coonawarra.name: Coonawarra
coonawarra.summary: Cool southern conditions and terra rossa soils produce structured Cabernet with signature mint and cassis.

cabernet-sauvignon.expect: Structured and cassis-driven, often with minty freshness and firm tannin.

identity.soil: Famous terra rossa red earth over pure limestone
influences: Cool maritime air from the Southern Ocean

why.effect: Produce the signature cassis-and-mint Cabernet profile
Retain acid structure and eucalyptus-fresh aromatics

margaret-river.name: Margaret River
margaret-river.summary: Ocean influence gives polished, aromatic wines with ripe fruit but notable freshness.

cabernet-sauvignon.expect: Polished Cabernet with cassis, bay leaf and cedar, balancing ripeness with freshness.

chardonnay.expect: Powerful yet taut Chardonnay, with citrus, stone fruit and savory oak.

why.effect: Polish ripe fruit while keeping freshness rare for the latitude
Tighten Cabernet's tannins and lift aromatic bay-leaf notes

stellenbosch.name: Stellenbosch
stellenbosch.summary: Warm sun plus cooling breezes produce ripe but structured reds and expressive whites.

cabernet-sauvignon.expect: Ripe and structured, with cassis, cedar and a distinctive herbal-savory edge.

syrah.expect: Dark-fruited and peppery, combining warmth with savory South African character.

chenin-blanc.expect: Textured and ripe, with quince, apple and waxy complexity held by Chenin's acidity.

why.effect: Slow ripening and preserve structure in warm-climate fruit
Contribute savoury fynbos and graphite complexity

maipo.name: Maipo Valley
maipo.summary: Sunny days and cool nights favor ripe Cabernet with herbal lift and firm structure.

cabernet-sauvignon.expect: Ripe cassis and blackberry meet minty, herbal freshness and firm tannin.

identity.terrain: Alluvial terraces fanning out from the Andes

why.cause: Pure Andean sunlight and warm days
why.effect: Ripen cassis to plush, dark concentration
Preserve the minty freshness typical of Chilean Cabernet

rheingau.name: Rheingau
rheingau.summary: A classic Riesling region known for more body and structure than the Mosel while retaining high acidity.

riesling.expect: More structured than Mosel Riesling, with citrus, stone fruit and firm acidity.

identity.terrain: South-facing slopes along a long river bend
influences: Taunus hills sheltering from north winds

why.effect: Ripen Riesling more fully than the Mosel, adding body
Retain acidity that keeps powerful dry styles balanced

clare-valley.name: Clare Valley
clare-valley.summary: Altitude and cool nights help preserve intense acidity in famously dry, lime-driven Riesling.

riesling.expect: Dry, piercing and lime-driven, often developing toast and mineral complexity with age.

identity.soil: Terra rossa over limestone pockets, slate in Watervale

why.effect: Preserve razor acidity in fully ripe Riesling
Build lime-and-toast intensity that ages for decades

sancerre.name: Sancerre
sancerre.summary: Loire Sauvignon Blanc at its most taut and mineral, emphasizing citrus, herbs and stony freshness.

sauvignon-blanc.expect: Lean, citrusy and mineral, with restrained fruit and herbal-flinty detail.

identity.terrain: Rounded hills on the upper Loire's right bank
identity.soil: Three soils: Terres Blanches chalk, Caillottes gravel-limestone, flint silex
influences: Chalk hills directly mining the same seam as Chablis

why.effect: Tighten Sauvignon Blanc into citrus, gunflint and smoke
Sharpen acidity well past herbal exuberance

vouvray.name: Vouvray
vouvray.summary: Chenin Blanc ranges from dry to sweet, united by high acidity, orchard fruit and strong ageing potential.

chenin-blanc.expect: High-acid and versatile, with quince, pear and honeyed complexity depending on sweetness and age.

identity.terrain: Plateau and slopes above the Loire with caves carved in tuffeau
influences: Harvest weather deciding sweet or dry
Limestone cellars cut into the cliff

why.effect: Give Chenin Blanc its chalky spine and quince fruit
Produce styles from bone-dry to botrytised sweet in one appellation

brunello.name: Brunello di Montalcino
brunello.summary: A powerful, ageworthy Sangiovese expression with more body, tannin and ripeness than Chianti Classico.

sangiovese.expect: Powerful and ageworthy, with cherry, plum, herbs, leather and firm tannin.

identity.terrain: A single hill (Montalcino) with varied exposures
identity.soil: Galestro marl in the north, clay and limestone in the south
influences: Mandatory long oak ageing by law

why.effect: Deepen Sangiovese's body and black-cherry concentration

why.cause: Required years in oak and bottle
why.effect: Develop leather, tobacco and dried-herb complexity

barbaresco.name: Barbaresco
barbaresco.summary: Nebbiolo with similar perfume and structure to Barolo, generally a little more approachable earlier.

nebbiolo.expect: Perfumed and structured, with rose, cherry and savory complexity, often slightly less forbidding than Barolo.

identity.terrain: Gentler slopes around a compact zone
identity.soil: Tortonian blue marl, similar to parts of Barolo

why.effect: Soften tannins and make Nebbiolo approachable earlier
Retain the rose, tar and truffle aromatic signature

southern-rhone.name: Southern Rhône
southern-rhone.summary: Sun-baked, herbal and generous, with Grenache commonly at the heart of blends.

grenache.expect: Warm, generous and herbal, with ripe red fruit, licorice and garrigue.

identity.soil: Red clay topped with rounded river stones (galets)

why.effect: Store heat and ripen Grenache to generous red-fruit ripeness
Mirror as herbal, thyme-and-lavender notes in the glass

champagne-blanc-de-blancs.name: Champagne — Blanc de Blancs
champagne-blanc-de-blancs.summary: Cool chalky Champagne preserves high acidity; bottle fermentation and lees ageing turn Chardonnay into a fine-bubbled, citrusy and increasingly brioche-like sparkling wine.

style.label: Sparkling · Traditional method
style.method: Second fermentation in bottle with lees ageing
style.effect: Bottle fermentation creates the bubbles; time on lees can add bread, biscuit and creamy texture while Chardonnay keeps citrus and chalky freshness.

chardonnay.ageing: Drink on release; fine examples can develop for 5–15+ years
chardonnay.expect: Taut, fine-bubbled and citrus-led, with chalky freshness and increasing brioche complexity from lees ageing.

why.effect: Keep the wine bright and precise despite the added texture of sparkling production.

why.cause: Second fermentation and maturation on lees
why.effect: Create persistent bubbles and can develop brioche, toast and creamy tertiary aromas.

prosecco-doc.name: Prosecco DOC
prosecco-doc.summary: Glera is made sparkling mainly through the Martinotti tank method, preserving pear, apple, citrus and floral aromas in a fresh, easy-drinking style.

style.label: Sparkling · Martinotti tank method
style.effect: Tank fermentation emphasizes Glera's fresh floral and orchard-fruit character rather than the stronger autolytic toast associated with long lees-aged bottle fermentation.

glera.expect: Light, lively and fruit-forward, with pear, apple, citrus and floral notes carried by gentle bubbles.

identity.terrain: Plains and hills across the DOC zone

why.cause: Glera's naturally fresh, floral fruit profile
why.effect: Provides pear, apple, citrus and blossom aromas.

why.cause: Martinotti second fermentation in sealed tanks
why.effect: Preserves primary fruit and floral character while creating the wine's bubbles.

cava.name: Cava
cava.summary: Traditional-method Cava combines bottle-fermented bubbles with Mediterranean fruit; Macabeo commonly brings freshness, floral notes and balance.

style.label: Sparkling · Traditional method
style.effect: Bottle fermentation and lees contact add texture and bread-like complexity while Macabeo contributes fresh fruit and floral lift.

macabeo.ageing: Best young to 5 years; longer-aged categories can develop further
macabeo.expect: Fresh, dry and fine-bubbled, with apple, citrus and floral notes plus subtle bread-and-almond complexity from bottle ageing.

identity.terrain: Especially associated with Penedès hills and plateaux
identity.soil: Limestone, clay and varied Mediterranean soils

why.effect: Brings delicacy, fruit and balance to traditional Cava blends.
Builds persistent bubbles and increasing lees-derived complexity with ageing.

sauternes.name: Sauternes
sauternes.climate: Moderate maritime with humid autumn mornings
sauternes.summary: Sémillon affected by noble rot becomes intensely sweet and concentrated, while acidity and Sauvignon Blanc in typical blends keep the style from feeling merely sugary.

style.label: Sweet · Botrytised
style.method: Noble-rot concentration followed by slow fermentation
style.effect: Botrytis dehydrates berries and concentrates sugar, acidity and aroma, creating honeyed, apricot-rich wines with saffron and marmalade complexity.

semillon.decant: No decant; older bottles may benefit from careful pouring
semillon.expect: Lusciously sweet yet structured, with apricot, honey, citrus preserve and saffron-like complexity.

identity.terrain: Gravel and clay-limestone slopes near the Garonne tributaries

why.effect: Dehydrates ripe berries, concentrating sugars, acids and distinctive honeyed, citrus-peel and spice aromas.

why.cause: Sémillon's texture and blending with fresher white varieties
why.effect: Produces richness with enough structure and acidity for long ageing.

tokaj-aszu.name: Tokaj — Aszú
tokaj-aszu.summary: Furmint's fierce acidity is the backbone of Tokaji Aszú, where botrytised berries deliver extraordinary sweetness, dried fruit, honey and spice without losing freshness.

style.label: Sweet · Botrytised Aszú
style.method: Selection of botrytised Aszú berries with slow fermentation and maturation
style.effect: Concentrated noble-rot fruit brings honey, apricot, citrus peel and spice while Furmint's high acidity keeps even very sweet wines vivid.

furmint.expect: Intensely sweet but electrically fresh, with apricot, citrus peel, honey and spice over Furmint's high-acid spine.

identity.terrain: Volcanic hills around the Bodrog and Tisza river confluence

why.effect: Balances the extreme sweetness and supports decades of ageing.

why.cause: Noble rot in suitable autumn conditions
why.effect: Concentrates sugars and creates dried-fruit, honey, tea and spice complexity.

douro-port-ruby.name: Douro — Ruby / LBV Port
douro-port-ruby.summary: Ruby-style Port preserves deep color and dark fruit; fortification stops fermentation while sugar remains, producing a powerful sweet wine with high alcohol and youthful fruit intensity.

style.label: Fortified · Ruby / LBV style
style.method: Fermentation stopped by grape spirit, followed by limited oxidative ageing
style.effect: Early fortification retains natural grape sugar and raises alcohol; relatively protected maturation preserves dark fruit, color and power.

port-blend.decant: LBV usually little or none; Vintage Port may need careful decanting
port-blend.ageing: Ruby/LBV is ready earlier; Vintage examples can develop for decades
port-blend.expect: Sweet, powerful and dark-fruited, with blackberry, plum and chocolate notes backed by warming alcohol and substantial structure.

influences: Shorter oxidative ageing than Tawny styles

why.cause: Fortification before fermentation has consumed all grape sugar
why.effect: Leaves pronounced sweetness while raising alcohol and preserving rich fruit.

why.cause: Ruby-style maturation with limited oxygen exposure
why.effect: Retains deep color and youthful blackberry, plum and chocolate character.

douro-port-tawny.name: Douro — Tawny Port
douro-port-tawny.summary: Tawny Port is fortified like other Port but spends longer in wood with controlled oxygen exposure, shifting the profile from fresh dark fruit toward nuts, caramel, dried fruit and spice.

style.label: Fortified · Oxidatively aged Tawny
style.method: Fortification followed by extended cask maturation
style.effect: Slow oxidation in wood softens color and tannin while developing walnut, caramel, dried-fruit and spice aromas.

port-blend.ageing: Ready to drink when bottled; age indication reflects cask maturation style
port-blend.expect: Silky, sweet and nutty, with fig, walnut, caramel and orange-peel complexity rather than the fresh dark fruit of Ruby styles.

why.effect: Encourages gradual oxidation and shifts fresh fruit toward nuts, caramel, dried fruit and spice.
Softens tannin and changes the color from ruby toward tawny and amber tones.

setubal-moscatel.name: Setúbal — Moscatel
setubal-moscatel.summary: Moscatel de Setúbal is an aromatic sweet fortified wine where grape spirit preserves sugar and prolonged contact with skins and later wood ageing can build orange peel, honey, caramel and nutty depth.

style.label: Fortified sweet · Moscatel de Setúbal
style.method: Fortification during fermentation, aromatic skin contact and maturation
style.effect: Fortification preserves natural sweetness; aromatic Moscatel character and maturation emphasize orange blossom, citrus peel, honey, raisin, caramel and nuts.

moscatel-alexandria.ageing: Young styles are aromatic and fresh; aged examples can develop for decades
moscatel-alexandria.expect: Richly aromatic and sweet, with orange blossom, candied citrus, honey and raisin; age can bring caramel, nuts and spice.

identity.terrain: Arrábida slopes and sandy plains around Setúbal

why.cause: Highly aromatic Moscatel de Alexandria grapes
why.effect: Give powerful orange-blossom, citrus and grapey perfume.
Preserve sweetness and can develop honey, caramel, raisin and nutty complexity.
